cyberattack: Bypassing bot protection or access controls
data.description:
The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control’s Surveillance Atlas provides infectious-disease surveillance data. Official description.
Our preserved Arquivo records contain 602 distinct timestamp-and-URL captures, representing 372 URL strings. 601 occurred on May 6–13, 2026, with one earlier capture on April 5. All belong to the SAWP5 user-initiated archiving collection. This identifies the archival workflow, not the requester or number of independent submissions.
Alongside ordinary API retrieval, the records contain encoded slashes, repeated slashes, an encoded parent-directory segment and a semicolon path variant. Examples include:
- /public/..%2Fpublic%2FAtlasService/rest/…
- /public/.;/AtlasService/rest/…
- /public/AtlasService%2Frest%2F…
These are consistent with attempts to change how intermediary or application layers interpret a URL. However, the records do not establish which security control, if any, the requester intended to bypass.
An ordinary health-topic endpoint returned HTTP 200 at 15:43:29 UTC on May 6; an encoded sibling-path variant returned HTTP 200 at 17:44:43. A previous audit recorded that both returned the same public catalog apart from a request identifier. The comparison bodies were not retained in the evidence available for this bundle, so that content comparison remains an auditor-reported observation rather than an independently reproducible body comparison. The semicolon variant returned 404.
Across the collection, 300 captures have indexed HTTP 200 responses. These statuses do not establish that every response contained usable data. The locally preserved bodies comprise a public dataset catalog and a 503 error page. No authentication bypass, protected-data access, successful WAF bypass or caused disruption is established.
The sequence is compatible with automated, potentially agent-driven retrieval, but requester and AI-provider attribution remain unconfirmed. Shared archive containers do not establish common authorship. A DeepSearchQA question concerns ECDC measles statistics, but an exact task match to this sequence has not been established.
data.summary: May 2026 archive captures show encoded-path and semicolon routing probes against ECDC’s (European Union) public Surveillance Atlas API. Some variants returned HTTP 200, but ordinary access also worked. No protected-data access or successful security bypass is established.
